Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Acute undifferentiated febrile illness for 1 week with rigors/chills, night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue; no focal respiratory, ENT, GI, GU, or skin symptoms. Recent travel to Vietnam with rural/farmland exposure; took malaria prophylaxis (drug unknown).  
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):  
  - Malaria (high likelihood): Travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; paroxysmal fevers and sweats; onset weeks after return; prophylaxis not fully protective.  
  - Enteric fever (moderate likelihood): Prolonged fever post–SE Asia travel with minimal localizing symptoms; GI features not reported but absence does not exclude.  
  - Common viral syndrome (moderate likelihood): Systemic symptoms compatible; healthcare worker exposure; lack of focal bacterial source.  
  - Others considered at lower likelihood per DDx: Dengue (timing less typical, no rash/retro-orbital pain), leptospirosis (no clear freshwater exposure or classic signs).  
- Working diagnosis: Acute febrile illness, cause undifferentiated; rule out malaria and other travel-related infections urgently.  
- Management priorities: Same-day in-person assessment and blood tests (including malaria thick/thin films and inflammatory markers); determine urgency based on examination; temporary work exclusion until diagnosis clarified.  

Management Plan

- Actions and recommendations:  
  - Same-day in-person clinic attendance arranged; administrative team to book; patient to call provided number to confirm.  
  - If unable to attend central clinic, attend local emergency department (A&E) with notes indicating need for malaria thick/thin films and inflammatory markers.  
  - Avoid work until clinical assessment and investigations clarify cause.  
- Follow-up: To be determined after in-person examination and initial test results.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Malaria (High): Travel to Vietnam with rural exposure; paroxysmal fevers/chills/sweats and myalgias; onset weeks after return; prophylaxis imperfect; malaria films ordered.  
- Enteric fever (Moderate): SE Asia travel with prolonged fever and few localizing signs; compatible exposure history.  
- Common viral syndrome (Moderate): Systemic symptoms without focal source; occupational exposure as a nurse.
